bug_info.bug_desc: In the old code, an accepted Advance command that completes with an invalid KMAC input does not commit the KMAC result into the internal key state because KeyUpdateKmac gates the key-state write with ~op_err. However, the FSM advance condition was only op_ack && advance_sel, so the working state still transitioned to the next key-manager state (e.g. StCtrlInit -> StCtrlCreatorRootKey, StCtrlCreatorRootKey -> StCtrlOwnerIntKey, StCtrlOwnerIntKey -> StCtrlOwnerKey) even though key_state_q was left unchanged. This leaves the new working state paired with the previous state's key material, which is inconsistent and violates the requirement that a command may advance only when the key state is successfully updated. The same fault exists in the three normal operational states that advance to a new key state.
bug_info.fix_hint: Introduce a key_update_vld signal that reflects whether the current update path actually overwrites key_state_d with the KMAC result. In KeyUpdateKmac, set key_update_vld = key_update & ~fault_err & ~op_err; in KeyUpdateInvalid, set key_update_vld = key_update. Then define next_state = op_ack && advance_sel && key_update_vld and use next_state for the advance-to-next-key-state transitions instead of op_ack && advance_sel. Keep the disable/fault transition to Disabled as invalid_state = op_ack && (disable_sel || fault_err). This ensures an invalid-input Advance cannot advance the working state without committing new key material.
